forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Reigate and Banstead faces £878k revenue overspend as property vacancies bite, while capital spending on track.
news_drafts.lead: Reigate and Banstead's first-quarter finances show a £878k overspend, driven almost entirely by empty commercial properties generating lost rental income. Redhill Distribution Centre alone accounts for £1,054k of the shortfall through vacancy, while The Rise and Regent House add further losses. Day-to-day spending on services, however, runs 1.6 per cent under budget when property is excluded, indicating core operations are tracking ahead of plan. The council has borrowed £13m so far this year for capital projects and cash flow, with further borrowing expected later. Its capital programme is on track to spend its full £33.8m budget with no slippage reported. A separate reserve-funded ash tree removal contract will exceed its initial £200k allocation, requiring additional draws from reserves.

findings.headline: Key projects workstream downgraded to Amber in LGR programme
findings.detail: One of four Local Government Reorganisation programme workstreams—Key projects/chunky business delivery—is now reporting Amber status, indicating deterioration from previous standing. Three workstreams continue to report Green. Expenditure remains within agreed budgets.
findings.matters: Deteriorating status on critical LGR preparation activity suggests potential delays in restructuring planning, which could have knock-on effects on service delivery and the council's financial position during transition.
findings.figures: 1 of 4 workstreams Amber; 3 Green; expenditure within budgets
findings.quote: Three of the four programme workstreams continue to report as Green, while the Key projects/chunky business delivery workstream is now Amber.

findings.headline: Council preparing for closedown activity in advance of Local Government Reorganisation Vesting Day
findings.detail: From August 2026, council is introducing a new workstream focused on closedown activity. The council has structured its internal work around the need to mitigate the strategic risk that LGR presents to delivery of corporate objectives in the period before Vesting Day.
findings.matters: A council in closedown ahead of restructuring faces distinct risks to service continuity and financial stability; lenders need visibility of LGR timeline and any financial implications.
findings.quote: From August onward a new workstream will be introduced, focusing on Council closedown activity; and the dashboard will therefore provide Members with an update on that in the future.

findings.paper_title: Addendum - OS Minute Q1 Revenue and Capital Budget 2026-27
findings.headline: Council projects a revenue overspend of approximately £878k by end of Q1 2026/27, primarily driven by loss of rental income from the vacant Redhill Distribution Centre.
findings.detail: Service budgets are forecasted to overspend by £906k, offset partially by a central budget underspend of £28k, resulting in a net projected overspend of approximately £878k for the year. The root cause is loss of rental income from the vacant Redhill Distribution Centre. The Property team is actively seeking new tenants to recover this income.
findings.matters: A material in-year revenue overspend of this scale requires either recovery action, spending controls, or reserve drawdown to balance the budget—concerns that would be material to a lender assessing the council's financial control and reserves position.
findings.quote: At the end of Quarter 1 there was an overall projected overspend against the original budget for the year of approximately £878k. The overspend was primarily due to loss of rental income from the vacant Redhill Distribution Centre. The Property team were actively seeking new tenants.

findings.paper_title: Housing Delivery on Council Owned Car Parks FINAL
findings.headline: Funding for feasibility and business case work is being drawn from the Feasibility Studies (Capital Schemes) Reserve, not from revenue or borrowing.
findings.detail: Para 9 specifies that 'Funding from the Feasibility Studies (Capital Schemes) Reserve, be used to complete the necessary work to progress the preferred option for each car park.' This suggests capital investment in exploratory work is being funded from reserves rather than from operating revenue or new borrowing.
findings.matters: Drawdown from capital reserves for exploratory work (advisers, feasibility studies, business cases) ahead of final decisions. Lender needs to understand the state of this reserve and whether funds are available for other capital priorities.
findings.figures: Not specified; amount to be determined
findings.quote: Funding from the Feasibility Studies (Capital Schemes) Reserve, be used to complete the necessary work to progress the preferred option for each car park

findings.paper_title: Housing Delivery on Council Owned Car Parks FINAL
findings.headline: All disposals exceeding £100,000 require approval from East Surrey shadow authority under section 24 Direction, creating dependency during local government reorganisation.
findings.detail: Para 49 states the council 'is unable to declare the Site surplus to requirements currently and agree to dispose of the asset without referral back to Executive for decision and subsequently to East Surrey Council's approval under section 24.' All decisions must be referred to the shadow authority. This adds a further gating condition to project execution at a time of significant organisational change.
findings.matters: Execution risk in a period of reorganisation. The shadow authority's approval is a prerequisite for disposal; non-approval could block the entire project or cause delays that affect timing of cash flows.
findings.quote: the Council is unable to declare the Site surplus to requirements currently and agree to dispose of the asset without referral back to Executive for decision and subsequently to East Surrey Council's approval under section 24
